nodes.description: ASPA gene replacement remains investigational. A 2023 expanded-access AAV9 case and a 2025 open-label rAAV-Olig001-ASPA trial support biological activity. The latter interim report included eight children with typical disease and found lower CSF NAA, increased myelin volume, and improved MSEL developmental scores against natural-history data. Gross-motor GMFM-88 slopes were not statistically significant. All participants had adverse events; seven had serious events, none attributed to the vector product, although procedure-related seizures and CSF leakage occurred. Small size, open-label design, historical comparisons, missing follow-up, and exclusion of atypical cases limit efficacy and durability conclusions. The AAV9 case corresponds to single-patient expanded access NCT05317780, listed by the registry as no longer available on 2026-10-04.

nodes.description: Approximately 2.6-kb SVA_E insertion in intron 4 of 5 of ASPA transcript NM_000049.4. In the 2025 series it was homozygous or in trans with another pathogenic allele. Long-read sequencing resolved the insertion; fibroblast RNA-seq supported a new splice acceptor, inclusion of SVA sequence, and transcript degradation. Population databases suggest a common pathogenic allele across ancestries, but this is not a disease-incidence estimate.

nodes.description: Partial inhibition of NAT8L-mediated NAA synthesis is a preclinical substrate-reduction approach. Genetic deletion and neonatal AAV-shRNA experiments rescued aspects of Aspa-deficient mouse pathology. Complete NAA ablation rescued myelin pathology but did not prolong survival in one double-mutant model, whereas partial reduction improved survival; these results caution against assuming maximal suppression is optimal. Human clinical benefit is unestablished.

nodes.description: ASPA-deficient mice show altered oligodendrocyte maturation, reduced myelin proteins, noncompact myelin, increased histone acetylation, and oligodendrocyte apoptosis during early postnatal development. These model findings establish cellular abnormalities but do not establish that histone acetylation or acetate shortage alone causes the human disease. In a separate nur7 study, oxidative stress preceded oligodendrocyte loss; ASPA overexpression partially rescued ATP under glucose deprivation in primary mouse oligodendrocytes, supporting a possible energetic contribution.
